title: Two Papers, One Error: A Category Mistake at the Foundation of the ISSN Diet Literature
content: The International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has published two documents on diet and body weight regulation: a position stand on diets for body weight reduction (Aragon et al., 2026) and a review of common questions and misconceptions about diets (Antonio et al., 2026). Both are thorough, evidence-based, and practically useful for their intended audience of coaches, athletes, and sports nutrition practitioners. Yet both contain the same category error at their foundation. The position stand calls the caloric deficit “axiomatic” – but a derived quantity cannot be an axiom. The review invokes the First Law of Thermodynamics as justification for the energy balance framework – but the First Law concerns energy, not mass, and says nothing about whether mass is primary or derived. In both documents, the same structural pattern appears: mass phenomena described in energy language, with logical contradictions following directly from the mismatch. This commentary presents the clearest contradictions from each document, with formal analyses derived from the energy balance framework’s own premises. The error is structural, not incidental. Both documents are already mass-based. Neither has yet named itself as one.
